incidents.event: Russia to Close Goethe-Institut Branches in Retaliation Against Germany
incidents.details: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Russia would close Goethe-Institut branches across the country in response to Germany’s measures following an explosives-laden drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

incidents.event: Russia Puts TV Propaganda Chiefs Under Guard Amid Threat of Ukrainian Strikes
incidents.details: Russia’s National Guard has stepped up security for senior television executives and prominent presenters, reportedly amid fears they could be targeted by Ukraine.

incidents.event: Tusk Calls Polish Drone Component Plant Fire Sabotage
incidents.details: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a fire at a WB Electronics plant producing components for unmanned systems was deliberately damaged in an act of sabotage and accused Russia of using cryptocurrency to finance the operation. Authorities have not reached the same conclusion, including a separate blaze at an aviation-components facility in Lublin.

incidents.event: Ukraine’s Drones Reach Moscow’s Doorstep, Hit Homes and Sochi Port
incidents.details: Russian officials say Ukrainian drones hit residential buildings in Moscow Region and caused a fire at a factory, while a separate attack hit the Black Sea port of Sochi.

incidents.event: Ukraine to Help Europe Close Defense Gaps as Russia Threat Grows
incidents.details: Ukraine will join a new European initiative to identify and rapidly address defense gaps, drawing on its battlefield experience against Russia. The effort comes as Europe faces Russian hybrid threats and uncertainty over the future US military role in NATO.

incidents.event: Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Region, Injuring 1 Amid Damaged Warehouses and Buildings
incidents.details: Russian forces attacked Kyiv region on Thursday, Sept. 3, injuring one person and damaging warehouses, an administrative building, a store, and kiosks. Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 163 drones overnight, with 135 shot down or suppressed.

incidents.event: EU Summons Russia Envoys, Eyes Sanctions After Germany Drone ‘Attack’
incidents.details: EU ministers agreed to advance sanctions against 1,600 Russia-linked individuals and entities after an explosive-laden drone incident at Leipzig airport. They also backed tougher Russian visa restrictions and discussed additional air-defense aid for Ukraine.

incidents.event: Leipzig Case Revives Push for EU Russian Visa Ban
incidents.details: A suspected sabotage plot at Leipzig airport is intensifying EU calls for tougher restrictions on Russian travelers. Ministers also debated the future of the EU’s foreign policy service and negotiations over the bloc’s next long-term budget.

incidents.event: ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 2, 2026
incidents.details: War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 2, 2026.

incidents.event: Germany’s Response to Attempted Russian Drone Attack at Leipzig Airport Criticized as Too Weak
incidents.details: Germany attributed the Leipzig/Halle sabotage plot to Russia but kept describing it as a hybrid attack, prompting criticism from Baltic and security officials.

incidents.event: Russian Strike Hits Multi-Story Residential Building in Odesa, Injuring 17, Including 3 Children
incidents.details: A Russian overnight air attack damaged a 21-story residential building in Odesa, injuring 17 people, including 3 children. Apartments on eight floors and several cars were damaged, while emergency and municipal crews continue clearing the aftermath.

incidents.event: Foreign Airlines Begin Suspending Flights to Russia Following Kyiv’s Warning That Its Airspace Is Unsafe
incidents.details: Airlines began canceling flights to Russia after Kyiv warned that expanding drone operations were making the country’s airspace increasingly unsafe for civilian aviation.

incidents.event: Zelensky Says Ukraine, Germany Finalizing Drone Deal as Kyiv Expands Defense Network
incidents.details: Ukraine and Germany are finalizing a bilateral Drone Deal covering joint production and defense cooperation, building on several projects already underway.

incidents.event: Norway Seizes Russian Ship to Enforce $4.2B Naftogaz Award
incidents.details: Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic at Naftogaz’s request as the Ukrainian energy company seeks compensation for assets illegally seized by Russia following its 2014 annexation of Crimea.

incidents.event: Ukraine Attacks Ship Used to Repair Key Black Sea Oil Moorings
incidents.details: Ukraine attacked a small service ship involved in planned  repair works at the key CPC oil terminal in the Black Sea, a person with knowledge of the matter said. The facility is vital to Kazakstan’s crude exports.

incidents.event: Dry Bulk Shipping Rates Surge on Tight Capesize Vessel Supply
incidents.details: A key measure of bulk-shipping rates has touched a two-year high and risks climbing further, according to analysts, as bad weather crimps the availability of Capesize vessels just as exporters ramp up delivery.

incidents.event: Container Spot Rates Hold Steady as Transpacific Gains Offset Asia-Europe Declines
incidents.details: Global container shipping rates held steady this week as stronger pricing on the Transpacific offset declines on Asia-Europe routes, according to Drewry. The Drewry World Container Index (WCI) was unchanged...

incidents.event: Global Containership Fleet Set to Hit Record 34 Million TEU
incidents.details: The global containership fleet is about to cross another major milestone, with capacity set to reach 34 million TEU after growing by 10 million TEU in just five and a...

incidents.event: REGENT Seaglider Takes First Crewed Flight in Major Step Toward Commercial Service
incidents.details: REGENT Craft has completed the first human-crewed flight of its full-scale Viceroy Seaglider prototype, a major milestone in the Rhode Island company’s effort to bring its unconventional high-speed maritime craft...

incidents.event: Global Marine Energy Leaders to Gather at IBIA Annual Convention 2026
incidents.details: IBIA – The International Bunker Industry Association will bring together leading figures from across the global marine energy and shipping industries at its 2026 Annual Convention, taking place 10–12 November at the New York Marriott Downtown. The Convention will address the key issues shaping the marine fuels sector, including regulation and policy, fuel quality, alternative ...

incidents.event: Ukrainian drones start fire at Russian oil export port
incidents.details: Ukraine’s relentless drone campaign has struck Russia’s Ust-Luga port, starting a massive blaze, and notching up its offensive against Moscow’s vital energy hubs. More than 52 drones and missiles were shot down over the Leningrad Region yesterday, its governor Alexander Drozdenko said on social media platform Telegram. “The drone attack caused damage to the Ust-Luga ...

incidents.event: Wheat Eases From 3-Year Peak
incidents.details: Wheat fell below $7.30 per bushel, easing from over a three-year high, amid expectations of a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine. President Putin stated there was a chance of a peace agreement to end the war with Ukraine, which triggered profit taking by traders. The EU also stated it was looking into “all possible ...

incidents.event: Precious Shipping continues fleet refresh with supramax sale
incidents.details: Thai dry bulk owner Precious Shipping has sold another ageing supramax for about $14.5m, pressing ahead with a fleet renewal drive that on the same day saw it take delivery of a new ultramax from China. The Khalid Hashim-led Bangkok-listed company is parting with the 2011-built, 56,920 dwt Kanchana Naree for about $14.6 m. The …

incidents.event: Suisse-Atlantique takes Chinese bulker orderbook to seven
incidents.details: Swiss dry bulk owner Suisse-Atlantique has expanded its newbuilding programme in China with two 40,500 dwt open-hatch ships, taking its orderbook at Jiangmen Nanyang Shipyard to seven vessels. The André family-controlled group confirmed the latest pair this week, adding them to five ultramaxes already contracted at the Guangdong yard. All seven ships are scheduled to …

incidents.event: Torvald Klaveness pockets $66m from KCC sell-down
incidents.details: Klaveness Combination Carriers’ largest shareholder has sold an 11% block in the Oslo-listed shipowner for about NOK619m ($66.5m), dropping below majority ownership while retaining a sizeable controlling position. Torvald Klaveness sold 6.54m KCC shares at NOK94.70 each through an accelerated private placement completed on Wednesday night. The sale was slightly larger than first planned. The …

incidents.event: Houthi fighters clash with Yemeni government forces in country’s southwest
incidents.details: Houthis attempt to cut road linking Taiz to al-Makha in apparent bid to sever government's strategic supply route.

incidents.event: Deadpool-Wolverine derby in the offing as Hugh Jackman targets Norwich City
incidents.details: After Deadpool actor Ryan Reynolds's purchase of Wrexham, his Wolverine costar could land Championship rivals Norwich.

incidents.event: How much oil is going through Hormuz? Why data doesn’t match US claims
incidents.details: Trump says the US is helping around 30 ships cross the waterway daily, but ship-tracking data suggests it's fewer.

incidents.event: Panama Canal restricts traffic amid Hormuz crisis: Why this matters
incidents.details: Limits on the number of vessels in the canal could create shipping delays and increase freight costs.

incidents.event: Iranian drone damages residential building in Kuwait City
incidents.details: An Iranian drone attack damaged a residential building in Kuwait, authorities say, with no casualties reported.

incidents.event: Somalia repels armed assault on Baidoa amid regional political tensions
incidents.details: Explosions and gunfire rock Baidoa as armed groups strike during South West State's political tensions.

incidents.event: Ukraine takes the war to Russia’s space programme in tactical shift
incidents.details: From Moscow to Plesetsk, Ukraine appears to be trying to hit infrastructure that powers Russia’s war from space.

incidents.event: Brazil Hands Government Control Over Mining Deals
incidents.details: Brazil's Congress passed a bill Wednesday letting the government block foreign takeovers of mining companies and scrutinize who gets access to the country's mineral reserves…the thing is, though...Brazil still can't turn its rare earth ore into a single magnet, and won't be able to for years. The Senate approved PL 2.780/2024 by voice vote, sending it to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for signature. It creates a national policy on critical and strategic minerals, a guarantee fund starting a

incidents.event: Machado Backs U.S. Oil Partnership but Questions Venezuela Deal
incidents.details: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado is backing a long-term U.S. role in developing the country’s oil reserves, even as she questions who has the authority to sign the sweeping agreement announced by acting President Delcy Rodríguez. Machado said Thursday that the scope of the agreement remains unclear, including who is signing it, who will finance it, what guarantees investors would receive and how Venezuelans would benefit. Those are fairly consequential blanks for a deal covering

incidents.event: Norway Seizes Russian Cruise Ship to Enforce Naftogaz's $4.22 Billion Claim
incidents.details: Norway has seized a Russian commercial cruise ship off the Svalbard archipelago at the request of Ukrainian oil and gas firm Naftogaz, which is seeking enforcement of a $4.22 billion award over Russia’s asset expropriation when it annexed Crimea. “At the request of Naftogaz Group, Norwegian authorities have seized the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov at the port of Barentsburg in Svalbard as part of global efforts to enforce the arbitral award obtained by Naftogaz and other Group companies aga

incidents.event: U.S. Diesel Prices Surge Toward All-Time High
incidents.details: The average price of diesel in the United States hit $5.7832 per gallon on Thursday, which is just three cents lower than the record-high of $5.8159 in mid-June 2022, when the Russian invasion of Ukraine sent fuel prices to record highs, data from AAA showed. The U.S. national average gasoline price is about $1 per gallon below the all-time high of $5.0165 from June 2022, but at over $4.10 a gallon now, the gasoline price is the highest it has been at this time of year, and is $1 higher than the

incidents.event: Russia’s Oil Revenue Sinks as Urals Falls to $59
incidents.details: Russia collected 326.2 billion rubles, or about $3.76 billion, in net oil revenue in August, down 22% from a year earlier and the lowest monthly total since February. Russia’s tax authority calculated August oil revenues using a crude price of just over $59 per barrel. Urals, Russia’s main export grade, averaged almost $95 per barrel during the spring after the Iran war pushed buyers toward barrels outside the Persian Gulf. Total Russian oil and gas revenue fell 16% year over year in August to 4

incidents.event: Russia Says Oil Output Drop Is Temporary as Refineries Restart
incidents.details: The dip in Russian oil production is only temporary, as output is expected to recover once refineries come back online after unscheduled maintenance, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Thursday. “This is a temporary phenomenon, and, generally, oil production will increase as the refineries resume operations and the situation stabilizes,” Novak said, as carried by Russian news agency TASS. Amid the ongoing fuel crisis in Russia, authorities have regularly sought to alleviate concerns a

incidents.event: EU Vows Tougher Russia Measures After Leipzig Drone Attack
incidents.details: The recent incident at Leipzig Airport in which explosive-laden drones interrupted flights is the "new normal," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on September 2, vowing more restrictive measures on Moscow. "Leipzig marks a new escalation on European soil, directly attributed to Russia," she said. "Every loophole Russia exploits is one we must close. We are looking at ways to cut even deeper into Russia's war chest." Von der Leyen was speaking alongside NATO Secretary Genera

incidents.event: Hormuz Disruptions Could Drag Into Next Year, Japanese Tanker Giant Warns
incidents.details: Japan’s Mitsui OSK Lines, the world’s largest tanker operator, expects the shipping disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz to continue for longer than previously expected, with no normalization by the end of the year, due to this week’s re-escalation of hostilities. “Given the current situation, it’s difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year,” Mitsui OSK Lines’ chief executive Jotaro Tamura told Bloomberg in an interview published on Thursday. In a quarterly financial

incidents.event: Iraq Hikes Oil Exports via Hormuz in Boon for Asian Refiners
incidents.details: OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq, more than doubled its crude oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz in August as it offered month-watering discounts for loadings at Basrah in the Persian Gulf and Iran allowed Iraqi oil cargoes to transit the chokepoint. Iraqi oil exports jumped to some 2.34 million barrels per day (bpd) in August from 1.35 million bpd in July, two Iraqi energy officials told Reuters, in data consistent with estimates of vessel-tracking firms Vortexa and Kpler, who see Iraq’s

incidents.event: Global Refining Crunch Could Keep Fuel Prices High Into 2027
incidents.details: Damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia and insufficient capacity elsewhere to offset the supply disruptions will likely keep global fuel prices elevated into the next year, analysts say. The Middle East conflict and the Iranian and Houthi strikes on Persian Gulf facilities have slashed supply and deliveries from the region, while intensified Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries have prompted a ban on diesel exports out of Russia. As a result, the global fuel markets are tightening,

incidents.event: Report to Congress on the U.S. Army’s Patriot Air and Missile Defense System
incidents.details: The following is the Aug. 27, 2026, Congressional Research Service report, U.S. Army’s Patriot Air and Missile Defense System. From the Report The Patriot air and missile defense (AMD) system is an Army ground-based mobile system designed to detect, track, and engage aircraft, uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), cruise missiles, and short-range or tactical ballistic missiles. Some Members of Congress have expressed interest in the cost, availability, and production of Patriot systems and intercepto

incidents.event: GE Aerospace to provide marine gas turbine engines for South Korea’s KDDX destroyers
incidents.details: It will supply 12 LM2500+G4 engines for six KDDX-class ships

incidents.event: Zelensky Discusses Support for Ukraine With Peru’s President Fujimori
incidents.details: President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori on Thursday, Sept. 3, for the first time since her inauguration in late July. He thanked her for her country’s continued condemnation of Russia’s invasion, and announced that the two also discussed bilateral trade and drone technologies.

incidents.event: India’s Double Game with Russia: Peace Rhetoric vs Record Oil Trade
incidents.details: While Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly urges Russian leader Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine, New Delhi is silently deepening its strategic and economic ties with Moscow. In this video, we break down the changing equation of India-Russia relations: from record-breaking Russian crude oil imports (exceeding 2.6 million barrels per day) to India supplying refined gasoline back to Russia, trade imbalances, and alternative transport corridors like the INSTC and Chennai-Vladivostok

incidents.event: 6 Wounded, Including a Child, in Russian Strikes on Kyiv
incidents.details: Russian forces struck Kyiv and the region on Thursday, Sept. 3, launching more than 163 drones overnight. One civilian was injured in the morning attacks, while the number of casualties in Kyiv rose to six later in the afternoon.

incidents.event: Russian House Shutdown: Decisive Move or Convenient Timing?
incidents.details: Berlin’s Russian House is the largest of a worldwide network operated by sanctioned Kremlin agency Rossotrudnichestvo. Critics accuse it of spreading propaganda, supporting Russian influence operations and using litigation to intimidate journalists. Germany has now announced its closure, but it is using an ordinary non-renewal clause that will not take effect until June 2027.

incidents.event: Russian Strike Injures 3, Damages Kyiv Apartment Block During Tuesday’s Barrage
incidents.details: A Russian strike damaged the upper floors of a 16-story apartment building in Kyiv’s Podil district, injuring three people. Firefighters rescued seven residents and extinguished a blaze that spread between two floors across an area of 100 square meters (1,076 square feet).

incidents.event: WATCH: Ukraine’s Khartiia Troops Break Through Near Kupyansk, Liberate Another 4 Square Kilometers
incidents.details: The 23rd Assault Regiment R.U.G. liberated another 4 square kilometers (1.5 square miles) in the Kupyansk sector, according to the Khartiia Corps. Ukrainian troops worked alongside the 35th Separate Marine Brigade during parts of the operation.

incidents.event: Ukraine Fast-Tracks Interceptors for Jet-Powered Shahed
incidents.details: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is accelerating development of high-speed interceptor drones to counter Russia’s jet-powered Shaheds. Ukrainian manufacturers have produced prototypes, while officials set deadlines to improve them and involve businesses in air defense production. Zelensky said Ukrainian intel knows Russia’s plans and that unspecified “asymmetric” operations have been approved.

incidents.event: SBU, HUR Offer Conflicting Accounts Over Kyiv Shootout
incidents.details: After a Kyiv shootout on Wednesday, the parties involved now offer conflicting accounts of what happened – the SBU accused an RDK commander (under HUR) of collaboration with Russia’s FSB, whereas the commander named said he was kidnapped, with the Russian plot being a cover-up for his abduction amid accusations of interagency rivalry.

incidents.event: Ukraine Official Says Strategic Attacks in Russia Could End Drone Terror
incidents.details: Counter-Disinformation Center chief Andriy Kovalenko said the only way to halt Russia’s drone attacks is to create comparable pressure at sensitive targets inside Russia. He rejected the idea that air defenses can instantly seal Ukraine’s skies, arguing that the threat must be addressed at its source. Kovalenko said disruptions at Russian airports will increasingly affect the country’s economy and daily life.

incidents.event: ‘Watch the News’: Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Teases New Momentum in Peace Talks
incidents.details: Andrii Sybiha said peace efforts could gain “new momentum” as political and diplomatic activity resumes in capitals around the world. He added that progress would be unrealistic without US involvement and urged people to “watch the news.”

incidents.event: Russian General Tied to Okhmatdyt Attack Reportedly Shot
incidents.details: A Russian Telegram channel claimed Maj. Gen. Nikolai Varpakhovich was shot twice outside a home in Saratov Oblast and remained in critical condition. The report has not been independently confirmed. Ukraine’s SBU alleges that Varpakhovich ordered and coordinated the July 2024 missile strike on Kyiv’s Okhmatdyt children’s hospital, which killed two people and injured dozens.

incidents.event: The Last Walk to Maidan: Remembering Eva Reuter
incidents.details: Eva Reuter, a 25-year-old artist-turned-combat medic with Ukraine's Hospitallers battalion, was killed rescuing victims of a Russian strike when attackers hit the scene again in a "double tap." Mourners gathered at Kyiv's St. Michael's Golden-Domed Cathedral before processing to Maidan Nezalezhnosti, where her fiancé, an American serviceman known as "Exile," delivered an emotional tribute to her courage and sacrifice.

incidents.event: Fuel, Energy Crisis in Strategic Russia-Occupied Crimea Worsening
incidents.details: Crimea is imposing tighter fuel rationing as Ukrainian strikes disrupt fuel deliveries. Stations will sell only four hours daily, while 20-liter and odd/even license-plate limits remain. Blackouts add to the peninsula’s growing crisis.

incidents.event: Putin Says Ukraine, Russia Must Reach Deal
incidents.details: Putin claims prospects for an agreement between Moscow and Kyiv still exist. A day earlier, he says Russia is refraining from targeting Ukraine’s leadership because it needs officials with whom it can negotiate.

incidents.event: ‘We Were Mistaken’: Putin Admits Russia Was Unprepared for Ukrainian Strikes on Oil Refineries
incidents.details: Putin has admitted Russia was “mistaken” in assuming its oil refineries would not be targeted, as Ukrainian drone strikes deepen a fuel crisis that has forced Moscow to turn to foreign gasoline imports.

incidents.event: ‘Enemy Did Not Take a Vacation’: Russia Escalates Attacks Across Ukraine, Zelensky Says
incidents.details: President Zelensky said Russia has launched a “new escalation” of its attacks, leaving damage across 13 Ukrainian regions overnight. A drone attack on a residential high-rise in Odesa wounded 17 people, including three children. Zelensky urged Europe to accelerate production of missile and drone defense systems as Russia increasingly deploys jet-powered drones.

incidents.event: Estonia’s Defense Minister Resigns Over Ukraine Ammunition Scandal
incidents.details: Estonian defense minister resigned after a €70 million ammo deal for Ukraine came under scrutiny and prosecutors opened a criminal investigation. Pevkur said he was taking political responsibility, although PM Michal said he saw no personal fault.

incidents.event: Drone Wall Rises: Ukraine Bets on Its Best Corps
incidents.details: A two-week roundup of the Russia-Ukraine war: Ukraine's 1st and 3rd Corps take command of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk defense, Russia launches a major ballistic missile strike on Kyiv, and Ukrainian forces hit a record 21 Russian oil refineries in August. Plus new weapons debuts, a Banderol missile strike on Pechenihy, and the latest on Russia's fuel and power shortages.

incidents.event: ‘No Scenario That Would Require It’: Putin Denies New Russian Mobilization – Again
incidents.details: Putin has again denied that Russia is preparing a new mobilization, calling the reports an “information attack” aimed at disrupting upcoming State Duma elections. His repeated denials come amid growing speculation that Moscow is preparing to expand military recruitment.
